options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Human females have a pair of X chromosomes (XX), so every egg receives an X besides 22 autosomes; there are no Y-bearing eggs (A false). R is true: having two sex chromosomes of the same type, the female is homogametic. It is the male (XY) that produces two kinds of sperms, X-bearing and Y-bearing, so the sex of the child is decided by the sperm.
steps: Female XX → all eggs carry X → A false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', sex determination: sex determination in humans
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: α-Thalassemia is observed due to mutation or deletion of one or more of the four genes HBA1 and HBA2 (two on chromosome 16 from each parent); the more genes affected, the fewer α-globin molecules are produced.
Statement II: β-Thalassemia is controlled by a single gene, HBB, on chromosome 11 of each parent and occurs due to mutation of one or both the genes.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Genetic basis of α- and β-thalassemia
solution.explanation: NCERT: α-thalassemia is controlled by two closely linked genes, HBA1 and HBA2, on chromosome 16 of each parent, and is observed due to mutation or deletion of one or more of the four genes; the more genes affected, the less α-globin is produced (Statement I true). β-Thalassemia is controlled by a single gene, HBB, on chromosome 11 of each parent and occurs due to mutation of one or both the genes (Statement II true).
steps: α: HBA1 + HBA2 on chr 16 × 2 parents = 4 genes
β: HBB on chr 11 × 2 parents = 2 genes
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', genetic disorders: Mendelian disorders (thalassemia)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Henking traced a specific nuclear structure through spermatogenesis in a few insects and named it the 'X body'. What did further investigations by other scientists conclude about it?

options.text: The 'X body' was in fact a chromosome, which is why it was given the name X chromosome
The 'X body' was a cytoplasmic granule unrelated to sex
The 'X body' was the nucleolus of the spermatocyte
The 'X body' was a Y chromosome that had lost its genes

solution.concept: From Henking's X body to the X chromosome
solution.explanation: NCERT: Henking (1891) observed that 50 per cent of the sperm received the X body after spermatogenesis and the other 50 per cent did not, but he could not explain its significance. Further investigations by other scientists led to the conclusion that the 'X body' was in fact a chromosome, and that is why it was given the name X chromosome.
steps: Later work: it is a chromosome
solution.why_others_wrong: The structure was shown to be a chromosome, not a cytoplasmic granule, a nucleolus or a Y chromosome.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', sex determination
solution.final_answer: Option A: The 'X body' was in fact a chromosome, which is why it was given the name X chromosome

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Genes A and B lie on the same chromosome, and the frequency of recombination between them is 20 per cent. A plant that received AB from one parent and ab from the other is self-pollinated. Assume the same recombination frequency in male and female gamete formation. What percentage of the progeny is expected to be aabb?

solution.concept: Gamete frequencies of a linked dihybrid
solution.explanation: With AB/ab and 20 per cent recombination, the gametes are parental AB 40 per cent and ab 40 per cent, and recombinant Ab 10 per cent and aB 10 per cent. An aabb plant needs an ab gamete from each parent: 0.40 × 0.40 = 0.16, i.e. 16 per cent.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1 per cent would apply if ab were a recombinant gamete (parents Ab/aB); 4 per cent squares the recombination frequency; 6.25 per cent (1/16) assumes independent assortment.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', chromosomal theory of inheritance: linkage and recombination
solution.final_answer: Option B: 16 per cent

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Suppose a polygenic trait is controlled by three genes A, B and C, and each dominant allele adds an equal amount to the phenotype. Plants AABBcc and aabbCC are crossed, and the F1 is self-pollinated. What fraction of the F2 will show a phenotype beyond (more extreme than) that of the parent with more dominant alleles?

solution.concept: Polygenic F2 can exceed the parental range
solution.explanation: The parents have 4 (AABBcc) and 2 (aabbCC) dominant alleles. The F1 is AaBbCc (3 dominant alleles). In its F2, the number of dominant alleles ranges from 0 to 6, with frequencies 1, 6, 15, 20, 15, 6, 1 (out of 64). More than 4 dominant alleles: 6/64 (five) + 1/64 (six) = 7/64.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1/64 counts only AABBCC; 15/64 is the class equal to the darker parent; 11/32 (22/64) includes that equal class as well.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', polygenic inheritance
solution.final_answer: Option C: 7/64

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
A man with normal colour vision and blood group AB marries a colour-blind woman with blood group O. Which of the following statements about their children are correct?

(a) All their sons will be colour blind.
(b) None of their children will have blood group O or blood group AB.
(c) All their daughters will have normal vision but will be carriers of colour blindness.
(d) The probability that their first child is a colour-blind son with blood group A is 1/4.
(e) Half of their daughters will be colour blind.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Combining an X-linked and an autosomal gene
solution.explanation: Colour vision: mother XᶜXᶜ, father XY (normal). Every son gets Xᶜ from his mother and Y from his father: colour blind (a). Every daughter gets Xᶜ from her mother and the normal X from her father: normal vision, carrier (c), so no daughter is colour blind (e false). Blood group: IᴬIᴮ × ii gives Iᴬi (A) or Iᴮi (B), each 1/2, never O or AB (b). First child a son (1/2, and then certainly colour blind) with blood group A (1/2): 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/4 (d).
steps: Sons: all colour blind; daughters: all carriers
Blood groups: A or B, 1/2 each
solution.why_others_wrong: '(a), (b) and (c) only' leaves out the true probability in (d); options with (e) are wrong because every daughter receives the father's normal X.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', sex-linked inheritance; co-dominance and multiple alleles
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Among the children of a man of genotype Iᴬi and a woman of genotype Iᴮi, all four blood groups, A, B, AB and O, are expected in equal proportions.
Reason (R): Each parent forms its two kinds of gametes in equal numbers; Iᴬ and Iᴮ are co-dominant while both are dominant over i, so the four equally likely genotypes IᴬIᴮ, Iᴬi, Iᴮi and ii each give a different blood group.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: All four ABO phenotypes from one couple
solution.explanation: Gametes: Iᴬ and i (1/2 each) from the father, Iᴮ and i (1/2 each) from the mother. The four combinations IᴬIᴮ, Iᴬi, Iᴮi and ii are each 1/4. Because of co-dominance (IᴬIᴮ → AB) and the recessiveness of i (Iᴬi → A, Iᴮi → B, ii → O), each genotype gives a different phenotype, so the four blood groups appear in a 1 : 1 : 1 : 1 ratio. R is exactly the reason for A.
steps: Each genotype → a distinct blood group
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of one gene: co-dominance and multiple alleles
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A couple with normal colour vision has a son with Klinefelter's syndrome (XXY) who is red-green colour blind. Assuming no new mutation, which explanation fits these facts?

options.text: A sperm carrying both the X and the Y chromosome of the father fertilised a normal egg carrying the colour-blindness allele
The mother is a carrier, and an egg carrying two X chromosomes, both with the colour-blindness allele, was fertilised by a Y-bearing sperm
An egg with no sex chromosome was fertilised by a sperm carrying both the X and the Y chromosome of the father
The father is a carrier of colour blindness and passed the allele to his son on the Y chromosome

solution.concept: Tracing an extra X chromosome with an X-linked marker
solution.explanation: Colour blindness is X-linked recessive, so an XXY son is colour blind only if both his X chromosomes carry the allele. The father has normal vision, so his X carries the normal allele; any X from him would make the son see normally. Both X chromosomes must therefore come from the mother, who must be a carrier (she sees normally); her egg had two X chromosomes (failure of segregation, aneuploidy) and was fertilised by a Y-bearing sperm.
steps: Son needs the allele on both X chromosomes
Father's X is normal → neither X came from him
Both X from a carrier mother + Y from father
solution.why_others_wrong: Any option in which the son receives his father's X gives him a normal allele; a male cannot be a carrier, and the gene is not on the Y chromosome.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', sex-linked inheritance; chromosomal disorders
solution.final_answer: Option B: The mother is a carrier, and an egg carrying two X chromosomes, both with the colour-blindness allele, was fertilised by a Y-bearing sperm

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Each dihybrid in List-I is test-crossed with aabb.

Match List-I (dihybrid test-crossed with aabb) with List-II (expected fraction of aabb progeny).

List-I:
A. AaBb, with the two genes on different chromosomes
B. A dihybrid that received AB from one parent and ab from the other, with 20 per cent recombination
C. A dihybrid that received Ab from one parent and aB from the other, with 20 per cent recombination
D. A dihybrid that received AB from one parent and ab from the other, with genes so tightly linked that no recombination occurs

List-II:
I. 1/2
II. 1/4
III. 1/10
IV. 2/5

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Test-cross outcomes with and without linkage
solution.explanation: In a test cross, the fraction of aabb progeny equals the fraction of ab gametes of the dihybrid. Independent genes: 1/4 (A-II). AB/ab with 20 per cent recombination: ab is parental, (1 − 0.2)/2 = 0.4 = 2/5 (B-IV). Ab/aB with 20 per cent recombination: ab is recombinant, 0.2/2 = 0.1 = 1/10 (C-III). Complete linkage of AB/ab: only AB and ab gametes, 1/2 (D-I).
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes confuse the coupling (AB/ab) and repulsion (Ab/aB) arrangements, or treat complete linkage as independent assortment.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', chromosomal theory of inheritance: linkage and recombination
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
In a bird species, the somatic cells of both sexes have 78 chromosomes. Which of the following statements are correct?

(a) The hen produces two kinds of eggs, each with 39 chromosomes: one kind carries a Z chromosome and the other a W chromosome.
(b) The cock produces only one kind of sperm with respect to the sex chromosomes.
(c) The sex of a chick is decided by the kind of egg that is fertilised.
(d) The somatic cells of the hen have 77 chromosomes, because she has only one Z chromosome.
(e) Each sperm of the cock carries 38 autosomes and a W chromosome.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: In birds the female is ZW and the male ZZ, so both sexes have the same number of chromosomes, 76 autosomes + 2 sex chromosomes = 78 (d false). The hen gives eggs with 38 autosomes + Z or 38 autosomes + W, 39 each (a). The cock gives only sperms with 38 autosomes + Z (b); it has no W (e false). Since the egg type varies and the sperm does not, the egg decides the sex of the chick (c).
steps: Hen ZW, cock ZZ: 78 in both
Sperms: 38 + Z only → egg decides sex
solution.why_others_wrong: (d) treats the ZW female like an XO male; (e) gives the male a W chromosome, which only females carry.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', sex determination
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The scheme of DNA replication in which each strand of the double helix acts as a template for the synthesis of a new complementary strand was proposed by:

solution.concept: Proposal and proof of semiconservative replication
solution.explanation: NCERT: while proposing the double helix structure, Watson and Crick also proposed a scheme for replication: the two strands separate and each acts as a template for a new complementary strand, so that each daughter molecule has one parental and one new strand (semiconservative). Meselson and Stahl (1958) later proved it experimentally in E. coli, and Taylor and colleagues showed it for chromosomes of Vicia faba.
steps: Proved in E. coli: Meselson and Stahl
solution.why_others_wrong: Meselson and Stahl and Taylor provided experimental proof; Hershey and Chase showed that DNA is the genetic material.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', replication: the experimental proof
solution.final_answer: Option A: Watson and Crick themselves

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, a nucleotide has three components. They are:

options.text: A nitrogenous base, a hexose sugar and a phosphate group
A nitrogenous base, a pentose sugar and an amino acid
Two nitrogenous bases joined by hydrogen bonds and a phosphate group
A nitrogenous base, a pentose sugar and a phosphate group

solution.explanation: NCERT: a nucleotide has three components: a nitrogenous base, a pentose sugar (ribose in RNA, deoxyribose in DNA) and a phosphate group. A base linked to the sugar is a nucleoside; adding a phosphate at the 5'-OH gives a nucleotide.
solution.why_others_wrong: The sugar is a pentose, not a hexose; amino acids are not part of nucleotides; hydrogen-bonded base pairs belong to the double helix, not to a single nucleotide.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', structure of polynucleotide chain
solution.final_answer: Option D: A nitrogenous base, a pentose sugar and a phosphate group

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The base sequence of an mRNA is the same as that of the coding strand of its gene, except that the mRNA has uracil in place of thymine.
Reason (R): The mRNA is synthesised complementary to the template strand, and the template strand is itself complementary to the coding strand.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Why mRNA matches the coding strand
solution.explanation: NCERT: in a transcription unit, the strand with 3'→5' polarity acts as the template, and the other strand, with 5'→3' polarity, has the same sequence as the RNA (except thymine at the place of uracil) and is called the coding strand. The RNA is built by complementary base pairing on the template; since the coding strand is also complementary to the template, the RNA and the coding strand carry the same sequence, with U in RNA where DNA has T. R is the direct cause of A.
steps: So RNA = coding strand (U for T)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', transcription: transcription unit
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: RNA, being a catalyst as well as genetic material, was reactive and hence unstable.
Statement II: DNA has evolved from RNA with chemical modifications that make it more stable.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: From the RNA world to DNA
solution.explanation: NCERT (RNA world): RNA was the first genetic material and used to act both as genetic material and as a catalyst. But RNA, being a catalyst, was reactive and hence unstable (Statement I true). Therefore DNA has evolved from RNA with chemical modifications that make it more stable; being double stranded, with a complementary strand, DNA further resists changes by evolving a process of repair (Statement II true).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', RNA world
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (enzyme or catalyst) with List-II (role).

List-I:
A. DNA-dependent DNA polymerase
B. DNA ligase
C. DNA-dependent RNA polymerase
D. 23S rRNA in bacteria (ribozyme)

List-II:
I. Joins the discontinuously synthesised fragments
II. Forms peptide bonds during translation
III. Synthesises RNA on a DNA template
IV. Polymerises deoxyribonucleotides on a DNA template

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Enzymes of replication, transcription and translation
solution.explanation: DNA-dependent DNA polymerases polymerise deoxyribonucleotides using a DNA template (A-IV). The discontinuously synthesised fragments of the lagging strand are later joined by DNA ligase (B-I). Transcription is catalysed by DNA-dependent RNA polymerase (C-III). In bacteria, 23S rRNA acts as the enzyme (ribozyme) for peptide bond formation (D-II).
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes swap DNA and RNA polymerase, ligase with the ribozyme, or the polymerase with ligase.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', replication: the machinery and the enzymes; transcription; translation
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-IV, B-I, C-III, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The pentose sugar present in the nucleotides of DNA is:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the pentose sugar is ribose in RNA and 2'-deoxyribose in DNA, which is why the nucleic acids are named ribonucleic acid and deoxyribonucleic acid. RNA retains a 2'-OH group on every nucleotide, which makes it labile; DNA lacks it.
solution.why_others_wrong: Ribose is the sugar of RNA, glucose is a hexose, and the missing oxygen in DNA's sugar is at the 2' carbon, not the 3' carbon.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', structure of polynucleotide chain
solution.final_answer: Option B: 2'-deoxyribose

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following nitrogenous bases are pyrimidines?

(a) Cytosine
(b) Thymine
(c) Uracil
(d) Adenine
(e) Guanine

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: nitrogenous bases are of two types, purines (adenine and guanine) and pyrimidines (cytosine, uracil and thymine). Cytosine is common to DNA and RNA; thymine is present in DNA and uracil in RNA.
solution.why_others_wrong: Adenine and guanine are purines, so options with (d) or (e) are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', structure of polynucleotide chain
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A mutant E. coli has an altered operator to which the lac repressor can no longer bind; its i, z, y and a genes and its promoter are normal. Glucose is absent. What happens in this mutant?

options.text: The z, y and a genes are never transcribed, even when lactose is present
The z, y and a genes are transcribed only when lactose is present, as in the wild type
The z, y and a genes are transcribed even when lactose is absent
Only the i gene is transcribed, and the repressor accumulates in the cell

solution.concept: Role of the operator in negative regulation
solution.explanation: In the lac operon, the repressor (from the i gene) binds to the operator and prevents RNA polymerase from transcribing the structural genes; the inducer acts by inactivating the repressor. If the repressor cannot bind the operator, nothing blocks RNA polymerase, so the polycistronic z-y-a mRNA is made whether or not lactose is present: the operon is expressed all the time.
steps: Repressor must bind operator to switch the operon off
Operator cannot bind repressor → never switched off
z, y, a transcribed even without lactose
solution.why_others_wrong: Nothing stops transcription in this mutant, so it cannot be 'never' or 'only with lactose'; the i gene is transcribed in the wild type too and its product simply cannot act here.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', regulation of gene expression: the lac operon
solution.final_answer: Option C: The z, y and a genes are transcribed even when lactose is absent

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): When the lac operon is switched on, the z, y and a genes are transcribed together.
Reason (R): In the lac operon, a polycistronic structural gene is regulated by a common promoter and regulatory genes.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Polycistronic organisation of the lac operon
solution.explanation: NCERT: in bacteria, the arrangement in which a polycistronic structural gene is regulated by a common promoter and regulatory genes is called an operon. The lac operon's structural genes z, y and a share one promoter and operator, so when the repressor is removed by the inducer, RNA polymerase transcribes them as one polycistronic mRNA. R explains A.
steps: One promoter for z, y, a
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', regulation of gene expression: the lac operon
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Because the bases pair in a complementary way, if the sequence of bases in one strand of a DNA double helix is known, the sequence in the other strand can be predicted.
Statement II: A circular double-stranded DNA molecule of 5386 base pairs has 10,772 phosphodiester linkages in all.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: base pairing confers a very unique property on the polynucleotide chains: they are complementary, so if the sequence of one strand is known, the other can be predicted (Statement I true). In a circular strand of n nucleotides there are n phosphodiester linkages (a linear strand has n − 1). Two strands of 5386 nucleotides each: 2 × 5386 = 10,772 (Statement II true).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', structure of polynucleotide chain
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: Human genome project and DNA fingerprinting
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the significance and findings of the Human Genome Project are correct according to NCERT?

(a) Knowledge about the effects of DNA variations among individuals can lead to revolutionising the ways to diagnose, treat and someday prevent thousands of disorders that affect human beings.
(b) Learning about non-human organisms' DNA sequences can lead to an understanding of their natural capabilities that can be applied to challenges in health care, agriculture, energy production and environmental remediation.
(c) Since less than 2 per cent of the genome codes for proteins, the remaining DNA has been shown to have no role at all.
(d) The human genome contains about 80,000 genes.
(e) The functions of all the discovered human genes are now known.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Why the Human Genome Project matters
solution.explanation: NCERT: knowledge about the effects of DNA variations among individuals can revolutionise the ways to diagnose, treat and someday prevent thousands of disorders (a); learning about the DNA of non-human organisms can lead to an understanding of their natural capabilities, applicable to health care, agriculture, energy production and environmental remediation (b). Repetitive sequences, though thought to have no direct coding function, shed light on chromosome structure, dynamics and evolution (c false). The genome has about 30,000 genes, not 80,000 (d false), and functions are unknown for over 50 per cent of the discovered genes (e false).
solution.why_others_wrong: Every other option includes at least one false statement.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', human genome project: goals, methodologies and salient features
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a) and (b) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (experiment) with List-II (label used).

List-I:
A. Hershey and Chase: labelling the DNA of bacteriophages
B. Hershey and Chase: labelling the protein coat of bacteriophages
C. Meselson and Stahl: replication in E. coli
D. Taylor and colleagues: replication in chromosomes of Vicia faba

List-II:
I. Radioactive thymidine
II. ¹⁵NH₄Cl as the only nitrogen source
III. Radioactive sulphur
IV. Radioactive phosphorus

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: DNA contains phosphorus but not sulphur, and protein contains sulphur but not phosphorus, so Hershey and Chase labelled phage DNA with radioactive phosphorus (A-IV) and the protein coat with radioactive sulphur (B-III). Meselson and Stahl grew E. coli on ¹⁵NH₄Cl as the only nitrogen source to make heavy DNA (C-II). Taylor and colleagues used radioactive thymidine on Vicia faba to detect the distribution of newly synthesised DNA in chromosomes (D-I).
steps: P in DNA, S in protein
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes swap the two Hershey–Chase labels or the two replication experiments.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', the search for genetic material; replication: the experimental proof
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a variation of Griffith's experiment, mice are injected with a mixture of heat-killed S strain and heat-killed R strain Streptococcus pneumoniae. What is expected?

options.text: The mice die, because the R strain is transformed by the S strain
The mice die, because heat-killed S strain bacteria alone are virulent
The mice live, because no living bacteria are present to be transformed or to multiply
The mice live, but living S strain bacteria are recovered from them

solution.explanation: NCERT (Griffith): live S strain kills mice; live R strain and heat-killed S strain alone do not. Only when heat-killed S was mixed with live R did the mice die, because the living R bacteria were transformed into virulent S bacteria. With both strains heat-killed, there are no living cells to be transformed or to cause infection, so the mice survive and no living bacteria can be recovered.
solution.why_others_wrong: Dead R cells cannot be transformed; heat-killed S alone is not virulent; and no living S cells can be recovered without living bacteria.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', the search for genetic material: transforming principle
solution.final_answer: Option C: The mice live, because no living bacteria are present to be transformed or to multiply

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
The template strand of a short stretch of a structural gene reads 3'-TACGAT-5'. Which of the following statements are correct?

(a) The mRNA transcribed from it reads 5'-AUGCUA-3'.
(b) The coding strand reads 5'-ATGCTA-3'.
(c) The first codon of the mRNA is the initiation codon AUG.
(d) The mRNA contains thymine at two positions.
(e) The RNA is polymerised in the 3'→5' direction.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: RNA is complementary and antiparallel to the template: template 3'-TACGAT-5' gives mRNA 5'-AUGCUA-3' (a). The coding strand has the same sequence as the mRNA with T for U: 5'-ATGCTA-3' (b). The first codon AUG is the initiation codon (c). RNA has uracil, not thymine (d false), and all nucleic acid polymerases add nucleotides in the 5'→3' direction (e false).
steps: Coding strand = mRNA with T for U
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) or (e) contain a false statement; '(b), (c) and (e)' also omits (a).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', transcription: transcription unit
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In eukaryotes, RNA polymerase I transcribes the rRNAs 28S, 18S and 5.8S, whereas RNA polymerase III transcribes the 5S rRNA.
Statement II: In eukaryotes, the heterogeneous nuclear RNA, the precursor of mRNA, is transcribed by RNA polymerase III.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Division of labour among eukaryotic RNA polymerases
solution.explanation: NCERT: in eukaryotes there are at least three RNA polymerases in the nucleus. RNA polymerase I transcribes rRNAs (28S, 18S and 5.8S); RNA polymerase III transcribes tRNA, 5S rRNA and snRNAs (Statement I true); RNA polymerase II transcribes the precursor of mRNA, hnRNA (Statement II false).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', transcription: transcription unit and gene
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In bacteria, the mRNA does not require any processing to become active.
Reason (R): Bacterial structural genes are split genes, with coding sequences interrupted by introns.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: in bacteria the mRNA does not require any processing to become active, and since transcription and translation occur in the same compartment, translation can begin before the mRNA is fully transcribed (A true). Split genes, with exons interrupted by introns, are a feature of eukaryotes; their hnRNA must be spliced. Bacterial genes are not split, so R is false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', transcription: transcription unit and gene; processing of hnRNA
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: One strand of a double-stranded DNA molecule has the base composition A 30 per cent, T 20 per cent, G 15 per cent and C 35 per cent. What percentage of all the bases in the double-stranded molecule is guanine?

solution.concept: Base composition of a double helix from one strand
solution.explanation: Each G in one strand pairs with a C in the other. The complementary strand therefore has G = 35 per cent (opposite the C of the first strand). Total G = (15 + 35)/2 = 25 per cent of the bases of the double helix. Check with Chargaff's rule: then C = 25, and A = T = (30 + 20)/2 = 25 per cent each.
solution.why_others_wrong: 15 per cent is the G of one strand only; 35 per cent is the G of the other strand only; 50 per cent is G + C, not G alone.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', structure of polynucleotide chain: double helix and Chargaff's rule
solution.final_answer: Option D: 25 per cent

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (E. coli strain (glucose absent)) with List-II (behaviour of the lac operon).

List-I:
A. Wild type
B. Mutant whose operator cannot bind the repressor
C. Mutant whose repressor binds the operator but cannot interact with the inducer
D. Mutant lacking the lac promoter

List-II:
I. Expressed only when lactose is present
II. Expressed even when lactose is absent
III. Not expressed even when lactose is present, because the repressor stays bound
IV. Not expressed, because RNA polymerase has no binding site

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Predicting lac operon behaviour in mutants
solution.explanation: Wild type: the repressor blocks the operator; lactose (inducer) inactivates it, so the operon is inducible (A-I). If the operator cannot bind the repressor, nothing blocks RNA polymerase and the genes are expressed even without lactose (B-II). If the repressor cannot interact with the inducer, it stays bound to the operator even when lactose is present (C-III). The promoter provides the binding site for RNA polymerase; without it, transcription cannot start (D-IV).
steps: Operator must bind repressor to switch off
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes swap the inducible and constitutive states, or the two non-expressing mutants, whose causes differ.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', regulation of gene expression: the lac operon; transcription unit
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
The coding strand of a short gene reads 5'-ATGGCATTCTAA-3'. Use: AUG = methionine, GCA = alanine, UUC = phenylalanine, UUU = phenylalanine, UAA = stop.

Which of the following statements are correct?

(a) The mRNA reads 5'-AUGGCAUUCUAA-3'.
(b) The polypeptide formed is methionine–alanine–phenylalanine.
(c) Deleting the fifth base of the gene would leave the amino acid sequence unchanged.
(d) Changing the ninth base of the coding strand from C to T would not change the polypeptide.
(e) The template strand, written 5'→3', reads 5'-ATGGCATTCTAA-3'.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Codons, mutations and the degenerate code
solution.explanation: mRNA = coding strand with U for T: AUG GCA UUC UAA (a): Met–Ala–Phe, then stop (b). Deleting the fifth base (C) gives AUG GAU UCU AA…: the reading frame shifts and the amino acids after the first change (c false). C→T at the ninth base turns UUC into UUU, which also codes for phenylalanine, since the code is degenerate (d). The sequence in (e) is the coding strand; the template, written 5'→3', is 5'-TTAGAATGCCAT-3' (e false).
solution.why_others_wrong: (c) ignores the frameshift caused by a single-base deletion; (e) gives the coding strand, not the template.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', genetic code; mutations and genetic code; translation
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: Human genome project and DNA fingerprinting
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): DNA fingerprinting uses repetitive (satellite) DNA rather than the protein-coding sequences.
Reason (R): Satellite DNA sequences show a high degree of polymorphism among individuals.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Why satellite DNA is used in fingerprinting
solution.explanation: NCERT: DNA fingerprinting involves identifying differences in some specific regions of the DNA sequence called repetitive DNA. Satellite DNA sequences normally do not code for any proteins, but they form a large portion of the human genome and show a high degree of polymorphism, which forms the basis of DNA fingerprinting. Since 99.9 per cent of the bases are the same in all people, it is the highly polymorphic regions that can tell individuals apart: R explains A.
steps: Satellite DNA is highly polymorphic → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', DNA fingerprinting
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
One DNA molecule of E. coli fully labelled with ¹⁵N (both strands heavy) replicates semiconservatively for several generations in a medium containing only ¹⁴NH₄Cl.

Given below are two statements:

Statement I: After any number of generations (one or more), exactly two of the descendant molecules are hybrid (¹⁵N/¹⁴N), and all the others are light.
Statement II: Heavy (¹⁵N/¹⁵N) DNA reappears after the third generation in the ¹⁴N medium.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Fate of parental strands in semiconservative replication
solution.explanation: In semiconservative replication the two parental heavy strands are never broken or lost; in each generation each one is paired with a new light strand. So after every generation exactly two molecules are hybrid and the rest are ¹⁴N/¹⁴N (Statement I true): e.g. 2 of 4 after two generations, 2 of 8 after three. A heavy/heavy molecule needs two ¹⁵N strands together, which cannot form in a medium supplying only ¹⁴N (Statement II false).
steps: Two parental strands persist, each in a hybrid
Hybrid count stays 2; light molecules increase
No new ¹⁵N strands → no heavy DNA
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', replication: the experimental proof
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A polypeptide of 150 amino acids is translated from an mRNA. What is the minimum length of the mRNA region from the first base of the start codon to the last base of the stop codon, and how many peptide bonds does the polypeptide contain?

solution.concept: Codons, stop codon and peptide bonds
solution.explanation: Each amino acid needs one triplet codon (the start codon AUG codes for the first methionine): 150 × 3 = 450 nucleotides. The stop codon codes for no amino acid but is part of the reading frame: + 3 = 453. A linear chain of n amino acids has n − 1 peptide bonds: 149.
solution.why_others_wrong: 450 forgets the stop codon; 150 peptide bonds counts one bond per amino acid instead of n − 1.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', genetic code; translation
solution.final_answer: Option C: 453 nucleotides; 149 peptide bonds

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Suppose Hershey and Chase had used bacteriophages labelled with both radioactive phosphorus (in DNA) and radioactive sulphur (in protein) to infect bacteria, followed by blending and centrifugation. Which results are expected?

(a) The bacterial cells in the pellet would carry radioactive phosphorus.
(b) Radioactive sulphur would be found mainly in the supernatant.
(c) Blending would separate the viral coats from the bacteria.
(d) Radioactive sulphur would be found inside the bacterial cells.
(e) The result would show that protein is the genetic material.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Only phage DNA enters the bacterium; the protein coat stays outside. Blending removes the viral coats from the bacteria (c), and centrifugation separates the light viral particles (supernatant, carrying ³⁵S protein) from the heavier bacteria (pellet, carrying ³²P DNA) (a, b). Sulphur-labelled protein does not enter (d false), so the result shows that DNA, not protein, is the genetic material (e false).
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) or (e) contradict the experiment's key finding that protein does not enter the cell.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', the search for genetic material
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: Human genome project and DNA fingerprinting
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (change in DNA or in the cell cycle) with List-II (consequence).

List-I:
A. A mutation in non-coding repetitive DNA that does not affect reproductive ability
B. Change of the sixth codon of the β-globin gene from GAG to GUG
C. Insertion of a single base within the coding region of a gene
D. Failure of cell division after DNA replication

List-II:
I. Polyploidy
II. Shift of the reading frame from the point of insertion
III. Glutamic acid replaced by valine in the β-globin chain
IV. Accumulation over generations, giving DNA polymorphism

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Mutations in non-coding DNA may have no immediate effect on reproductive ability, so they accumulate generation after generation, one cause of DNA polymorphism (A-IV). GAG→GUG at the sixth codon of β-globin replaces glutamic acid by valine, causing sickle-cell anaemia (B-III). A single-base insertion shifts the reading frame (C-II). NCERT: a failure in cell division after DNA replication results in polyploidy (D-I).
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes swap the substitution with the frameshift, or polyploidy with polymorphism.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', DNA fingerprinting; mutations and genetic code; replication
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about events at a replication fork are correct?

(a) On the template strand with 3'→5' polarity, the new strand is synthesised continuously.
(b) On the template strand with 5'→3' polarity, the new strand is synthesised discontinuously.
(c) The discontinuously synthesised fragments are later joined by DNA ligase.
(d) DNA polymerase can initiate replication at any random place in the DNA.
(e) The new strands are polymerised in the 3'→5' direction.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: DNA-dependent DNA polymerases catalyse polymerisation only in the 5'→3' direction. Consequently, on the template with 3'→5' polarity replication is continuous (a), while on the template with 5'→3' polarity it is discontinuous (b); the fragments are joined by DNA ligase (c). Replication does not start randomly: it begins at a definite region, the origin of replication (d false). Polymerisation is 5'→3', not 3'→5' (e false).
steps: Ligase joins fragments; start at origin
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) or (e) contain a false statement.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', replication: the machinery and the enzymes
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: NCERT points out that microbes are present everywhere. Which of the following places does it name as habitats where microbes are found?

options.text: Only in soil, water and air, never inside the bodies of animals and plants
Thermal vents (where the temperature may be as high as 100 °C), deep in the soil, under layers of snow and highly acidic environments
Only in moderate environments, never above 50 °C or in acidic conditions
Only inside the bodies of animals and plants, never free in nature

solution.explanation: NCERT: microbes are present everywhere: in soil, water and air, inside our bodies and those of other animals and plants, and even where no other life form could possibly exist, such as deep inside geysers (thermal vents) where the temperature may be as high as 100 °C, deep in the soil, under the layers of snow several metres thick, and in highly acidic environments.
steps: Everywhere: soil, water, air, inside organisms
Extreme habitats: thermal vents up to 100 °C, deep soil, under snow, acidic places
solution.why_others_wrong: Each wrong option restricts microbes to some habitats, whereas NCERT stresses that they are found everywhere, including inside bodies and in extreme environments.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', introduction
solution.final_answer: Option B: Thermal vents (where the temperature may be as high as 100 °C), deep in the soil, under layers of snow and highly acidic environments

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a sewage treatment plant, the secondary treatment, in which the primary effluent is passed into aeration tanks and microbes consume its organic matter, is also called:

solution.explanation: NCERT: primary treatment involves the physical removal of particles (filtration and sedimentation). Secondary treatment, or biological treatment, uses the vigorous growth of useful aerobic microbes into flocs in the aeration tanks; these consume the major part of the organic matter and reduce the BOD of the effluent.
steps: Secondary: microbes digest organic matter = biological treatment
solution.why_others_wrong: Physical removal is primary treatment; NCERT does not describe the aeration step as chemical or tertiary treatment.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes in sewage treatment: secondary treatment
solution.final_answer: Option D: Biological treatment

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Microbes such as bacteria and fungi can be grown on nutritive media to form colonies that can be seen with the naked eye.
Statement II: Prions, mentioned by NCERT among the diverse microbes, are proteinaceous infectious agents.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: microbes are diverse: protozoa, bacteria, fungi, microscopic plant and animal viruses, viroids and also prions, which are proteinaceous infectious agents (Statement II true). Microbes like bacteria and many fungi can be grown on nutritive media to form colonies that can be seen with the naked eye, and such cultures are useful in studies on micro-organisms (Statement I true).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', introduction
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Biofertilisers are not yet available commercially in India, so farmers cannot use them in their fields.
Reason (R): Biofertilisers are organisms that enrich the nutrient quality of the soil.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: biofertilisers are organisms that enrich the nutrient quality of the soil; the main sources are bacteria, fungi and cyanobacteria (R true). Currently, in our country, a number of biofertilisers are available commercially in the market, and farmers use these regularly in their fields to replenish soil nutrients and to reduce dependence on chemical fertilisers. So A is false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes as biofertilisers
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements are correct according to NCERT?

(a) The excreta of cattle, rich in methanogenic bacteria, is used to generate biogas, commonly called gobar gas.
(b) Rhizobium fixes atmospheric nitrogen in symbiotic association with the root nodules of leguminous plants.
(c) Cyanobacteria are autotrophic microbes widely distributed in aquatic and terrestrial environments.
(d) Methanogens grow aerobically and need constant aeration.
(e) Mycorrhizal fungi such as Glomus fix atmospheric nitrogen for the plant.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Microbes in biogas and as biofertilisers
solution.explanation: Cattle excreta (gobar), rich in methanogens, is used for biogas, commonly called gobar gas (a). The bacteria forming nodules on the roots of leguminous plants by symbiotic association are Rhizobium, which fix atmospheric nitrogen (b). Cyanobacteria are autotrophic microbes widely distributed in aquatic and terrestrial environments, many of which fix nitrogen (c). Methanogens grow anaerobically (d false). Glomus forms mycorrhiza and absorbs phosphorus from the soil for the plant; it is not described as fixing nitrogen (e false).
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) or (e) contain a false statement; '(a), (c) and (d)' also omits (b).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes in production of biogas; microbes as biofertilisers
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In primary treatment, all the solids that settle form the primary sludge, and the supernatant forms the effluent, which is taken for secondary treatment.
Statement II: Once the BOD has been reduced in the aeration tanks, the effluent is released directly into rivers without being passed through any settling tank.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Sludge and effluent in sewage treatment
solution.explanation: NCERT: after filtration and sedimentation in primary treatment, all solids that settle form the primary sludge, and the supernatant forms the effluent, which goes for secondary treatment (Statement I true). Once the BOD is reduced significantly, the effluent is passed into a settling tank where the bacterial flocs sediment as activated sludge; only then is the effluent from secondary treatment released into natural water bodies (Statement II false).
steps: Settling tank comes before release → Statement II false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes in sewage treatment
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (biocontrol agent) with List-II (pest or pathogen it controls).

List-I:
A. Ladybird beetle
B. Dragonflies
C. Bacillus thuringiensis
D. Trichoderma

List-II:
I. Several plant pathogens
II. Aphids
III. Mosquitoes
IV. Butterfly caterpillars

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Matching biocontrol agents with their targets
solution.explanation: NCERT: the ladybird and dragonflies are useful to get rid of aphids and mosquitoes, respectively (A-II, B-III). Bacillus thuringiensis is used to control butterfly caterpillars (C-IV). Trichoderma species are free-living fungi that are effective biocontrol agents of several plant pathogens (D-I).
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes swap the targets of the ladybird and dragonflies, of Bt and Trichoderma, or of the ladybird and Bt.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes as biocontrol agents
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Baculoviruses of the genus Nucleopolyhedrovirus are desirable for biological control in an integrated pest management programme in which beneficial insects are being conserved.
Reason (R): These viruses are species-specific, narrow-spectrum insecticidal agents with no negative impact on plants, mammals, birds, fish or even non-target insects.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Why baculoviruses suit integrated pest management
solution.explanation: NCERT: baculoviruses (mostly genus Nucleopolyhedrovirus) attack insects and other arthropods. They have been shown to have no negative impacts on plants, mammals, birds, fish or even on non-target insects. This is especially desirable when beneficial insects are being conserved to aid an overall IPM programme, or when an ecologically sensitive area is being treated. Their species-specific, narrow-spectrum action is the reason for A.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes as biocontrol agents
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about microbes in household and industrial products are correct?

(a) Both the large holes in Swiss cheese and the puffed-up appearance of dosa and idli dough result from carbon dioxide produced by microbes.
(b) Whisky is produced by distillation of the fermented broth, whereas wine is produced without distillation.
(c) Lactic acid bacteria convert milk to curd and also increase its vitamin B₁₂ content.
(d) Roquefort cheese is ripened by growing a specific bacterium on it.
(e) Citric acid is produced commercially by the bacterium Acetobacter aceti.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Propionibacterium sharmanii produces a large amount of CO₂ that makes the holes in Swiss cheese, and the dough for dosa and idli puffs up due to CO₂ produced by bacteria (a). Wine and beer are produced without distillation, whereas whisky, brandy and rum are produced by distillation of the fermented broth (b). LAB convert milk to curd and improve its nutritional quality by increasing vitamin B₁₂ (c). Roquefort cheese is ripened by a specific fungus (d false), and citric acid comes from the fungus Aspergillus niger, while Acetobacter aceti makes acetic acid (e false).
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) or (e) contain a false statement; '(b), (c) and (d)' also omits (a).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes in household products; microbes in industrial products
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which pair of products are both obtained from bacteria, according to NCERT?

solution.explanation: Streptokinase is produced by the bacterium Streptococcus, and butyric acid by the bacterium Clostridium butylicum. Cyclosporin A comes from the fungus Trichoderma polysporum and citric acid from the fungus Aspergillus niger; statins come from the fungus Monascus purpureus and ethanol is produced commercially using the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae; penicillin comes from the mould Penicillium notatum.
solution.why_others_wrong: Each of the other pairs contains products of fungi or yeasts only.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes in industrial products
solution.final_answer: Option D: Streptokinase and butyric acid

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, populations evolve to maximise their reproductive fitness, also called Darwinian fitness, in the habitat in which they live. Such fitness is indicated by:

options.text: A high carrying capacity K of the habitat
A high value of r, the intrinsic rate of natural increase
A large body size of the individuals

solution.explanation: NCERT (life history variation): populations evolve to maximise their reproductive fitness, also called Darwinian fitness (high r value), in the habitat in which they live. r is the intrinsic rate of natural increase, the parameter NCERT also uses to assess the impact of any factor on population growth.
solution.why_others_wrong: K is a property of the habitat, a high death rate lowers r, and NCERT does not equate fitness with body size.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', populations: life history variation
solution.final_answer: Option B: A high value of r, the intrinsic rate of natural increase

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In amensalism, both interacting species benefit.
Reason (R): In commensalism, one species benefits and the other is neither harmed nor benefited.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: in amensalism one species is harmed whereas the other is unaffected; it is not an interaction in which both benefit (that is mutualism), so A is false. Commensalism is the interaction in which one species benefits and the other is neither harmed nor benefited, as with an orchid growing as an epiphyte on a mango branch (R true).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', populations: population interactions
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (term) with List-II (meaning).

List-I:
A. Carrying capacity (K)
B. Intrinsic rate of natural increase (r)
C. Age pyramid
D. Population density

List-II:
I. Per capita birth rate minus per capita death rate (b − d)
II. Size of a population per unit area, as numbers, biomass or per cent cover
III. Maximum number of individuals that the habitat can support
IV. Plot of the age distribution of a population

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Carrying capacity K is the limit beyond which no further growth is possible, the maximum the habitat's resources can support (A-III). In dN/dt = (b − d)N, r = b − d is the intrinsic rate of natural increase (B-I). Plotting the per cent of individuals in each age group gives the age pyramid (C-IV). Population density is population size per unit area, measured as numbers, biomass or per cent cover (D-II).
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes swap K with r, the age pyramid with density, or r with the age pyramid.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', populations: population attributes; population growth
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Some organisms breed only once in their lifetime, such as Pacific salmon fish and bamboo, while others breed many times during their lifetime, such as most birds and mammals.
Statement II: Some organisms produce a large number of small-sized offspring, such as oysters and pelagic fishes, while others produce a small number of large-sized offspring, such as birds and mammals.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: under a particular set of selection pressures, organisms evolve towards the most efficient reproductive strategy. Some breed only once in their lifetime (Pacific salmon fish, bamboo), while others breed many times (most birds and mammals) (Statement I true). Some produce a large number of small-sized offspring (oysters, pelagic fishes), while others produce a small number of large-sized offspring (birds, mammals) (Statement II true).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', populations: life history variation
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A population growing in a habitat with limited resources shows a deceleration phase as its density approaches the carrying capacity.
Reason (R): In the logistic equation dN/dt = rN[(K − N)/K], the factor (K − N)/K becomes smaller as N increases, lowering the growth rate per individual.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: In logistic growth the per capita growth rate is r(K − N)/K. As N rises towards K, (K − N)/K falls towards zero, so each individual contributes less and less to growth: the curve passes from acceleration into deceleration and finally reaches an asymptote at K. R is the mathematical reason for A.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', populations: population growth (logistic growth)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A population grows according to the logistic model, dN/dt = rN[(K − N)/K], with r = 0.4 per year and K = 2000. At what population size is the growth rate dN/dt the highest, and what is that rate?

solution.concept: Maximum growth rate in logistic growth
solution.explanation: dN/dt = rN(K − N)/K is a product that is largest when N = K/2 (the middle of the S-shaped curve). Here N = 2000/2 = 1000, and dN/dt = 0.4 × 1000 × (2000 − 1000)/2000 = 0.4 × 1000 × 0.5 = 200 individuals per year (the maximum, rK/4).
solution.why_others_wrong: At N = K growth is zero, not maximum; 400 forgets the (K − N)/K factor; at N = 500 the rate is 0.4 × 500 × 0.75 = 150, which is less than 200.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', populations: population growth (logistic growth)
solution.final_answer: Option D: At N = 1000; 200 individuals per year

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about life history variation are correct according to NCERT?

(a) Under a particular set of selection pressures, organisms evolve towards the most efficient reproductive strategy.
(b) Ecologists suggest that life history traits of organisms have evolved in relation to the constraints imposed by the abiotic and biotic components of the habitat.
(c) All populations have the same intrinsic rate of natural increase.
(d) The number and size of offspring are the same in all species.
(e) Life history traits do not depend in any way on the habitat.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: populations evolve to maximise reproductive fitness in their habitat; under a particular set of selection pressures, organisms evolve towards the most efficient reproductive strategy (a), and ecologists suggest that life history traits have evolved in relation to the constraints imposed by the abiotic and biotic components of the habitat (b). NCERT's r values differ widely (0.12 for the flour beetle, 0.015 for the Norway rat) (c false); species differ in the number and size of their offspring (d false); and life history traits are shaped by the habitat (e false).
solution.why_others_wrong: Every other option includes at least one false statement.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', populations: life history variation
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a) and (b) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: For a population growing exponentially (dN/dt = rN) with a constant r, what is the shape of the graph of the growth rate dN/dt plotted against population size N?

options.text: A horizontal straight line, since dN/dt stays constant
A bell-shaped curve with its peak at N = K/2
A straight line through the origin, with slope r
An S-shaped curve that levels off at K

solution.explanation: In dN/dt = rN, dN/dt is directly proportional to N with constant r, so the graph of dN/dt against N is a straight line through the origin with slope r: the bigger the population, the faster it grows (this is why N plotted against time gives a J-shaped curve). A hump-shaped dN/dt with a peak at K/2 belongs to logistic growth, and the S-shaped curve is N against time in logistic growth.
steps: Straight line through origin, slope r
solution.why_others_wrong: dN/dt is not constant (it rises with N); the peak at K/2 and the S-shape belong to logistic growth.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', populations: population growth (exponential growth)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A straight line through the origin, with slope r

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: When certain exotic species are introduced into a geographical area, they may become invasive and spread fast, because the invaded land does not have their natural predators.
Statement II: Predators always drive their prey species to extinction.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: one reason why certain exotic species become invasive and spread fast when introduced into a geographical area is that the invaded land does not have their natural predators, as with the prickly pear cactus in Australia (Statement I true). Predators in nature are 'prudent': a predator that overexploits its prey might itself become extinct for lack of food, and predators keep prey populations under control rather than eliminating them (Statement II false).
steps: Prudent predators; prey kept under control → Statement II false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', populations: population interactions (predation)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about plant defences against herbivores are correct?

(a) Thorns, as in Acacia and cactus, are the most common morphological means of defence.
(b) Many plants produce and store chemicals that make the herbivore sick when eaten, inhibit feeding or digestion, disrupt its reproduction or even kill it.
(c) Nicotine, caffeine, quinine, strychnine and opium are produced by plants as defences against grazers and browsers.
(d) Plants produce these chemicals mainly to attract herbivores.
(e) Calotropis is heavily browsed by cattle and goats.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Morphological and chemical defences of plants
solution.explanation: NCERT: since plants cannot run away, they have evolved morphological and chemical defences. Thorns (Acacia, cactus) are the most common morphological means of defence (a). Many plants produce and store chemicals that make the herbivore sick, inhibit feeding or digestion, disrupt reproduction or kill it (b); nicotine, caffeine, quinine, strychnine and opium are such defences (c). These chemicals deter rather than attract herbivores (d false), and Calotropis produces highly poisonous cardiac glycosides, so cattle and goats never browse on it (e false).
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) or (e) contain a false statement; '(b), (c) and (d)' also omits (a).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', populations: population interactions (predation)
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
For a population with r = 0.2 per year, compare the exponential model dN/dt = rN with the logistic model dN/dt = rN[(K − N)/K], taking K = 1000.

Match List-I (model and population size) with List-II (growth rate (individuals per year)).

List-I:
A. Exponential, N = 400
B. Logistic, N = 400
C. Logistic, N = 900
D. Logistic, N = 1000

List-II:
I. 0
II. 18
III. 48
IV. 80

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Exponential and logistic growth rates compared
solution.explanation: Exponential: 0.2 × 400 = 80 (A-IV). Logistic at 400: 0.2 × 400 × 600/1000 = 48 (B-III). Logistic at 900: 0.2 × 900 × 100/1000 = 18 (C-II). At N = K = 1000: 0.2 × 1000 × 0 = 0; the population has reached its asymptote (D-I).
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes swap the exponential and logistic values at N = 400, or the logistic values at 900 and 1000.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', populations: population growth
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
The age structure of three populations is: P: pre-reproductive 45 per cent, reproductive 40 per cent, post-reproductive 15 per cent; Q: 35, 36 and 29 per cent; R: 15, 45 and 40 per cent.

Which of the following inferences are correct?

(a) The age pyramid of P has a broad base and indicates an expanding population.
(b) The age pyramid of R is urn-shaped and indicates a declining population.
(c) The age pyramid of Q is bell-shaped and indicates a stable population.
(d) Population P is declining, since its post-reproductive group is the smallest.
(e) Population R has the broadest base of the three pyramids.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The shape of the age pyramid reflects the growth status of a population. P has more pre-reproductive than reproductive individuals: broad base, expanding (a). R has far fewer pre-reproductive than reproductive individuals: narrow base, urn-shaped, declining (b). In Q the pre-reproductive and reproductive groups are nearly equal: bell-shaped, stable (c). A small post-reproductive group does not make P decline (d false), and R has the narrowest, not the broadest, base (e false).
solution.why_others_wrong: (d) judges growth from the post-reproductive group; (e) reverses the base widths.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', populations: population attributes (age pyramids)
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Two populations of the same species grow exponentially with the same r = 0.02 per year: one starts with 100 individuals and the other with 10,000. Which statement about the time each takes to double is correct? (Nₜ = N₀e^(rt); ln 2 = 0.693)

options.text: The smaller population doubles 100 times faster
The larger population doubles 100 times faster
The doubling times cannot be compared without knowing the carrying capacity
Both take the same time, about 35 years, because the doubling time depends only on r

solution.explanation: Doubling means Nₜ = 2N₀: 2N₀ = N₀e^(rt), so e^(rt) = 2 and t = ln 2/r = 0.693/0.02 ≈ 34.7 years. N₀ cancels: under exponential growth, every population with the same r doubles in the same time, whatever its starting size, although the larger population adds far more individuals in that time.
solution.why_others_wrong: Starting size does not affect the doubling time in the exponential model, and K does not appear in it.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', populations: population growth (exponential growth)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Both take the same time, about 35 years, because the doubling time depends only on r

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Write the effect of an interaction on each partner as + (benefit), − (harm) or 0 (no effect).

Which of the following pairings are correct?

(a) Fig and its pollinating wasp: (+, +)
(b) Cattle egret and grazing cattle: (+, 0)
(c) Orchid growing as an epiphyte and the mango branch it grows on: (+, 0)
(d) Cuscuta and the hedge plant on which it grows: (+, 0)
(e) Clown fish and the sea anemone among whose tentacles it lives: (+, +)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Fig and wasp: the wasp pollinates the fig while using its fruit for egg laying and larval food; both benefit, mutualism (a). Cattle egrets catch insects stirred up by cattle, which are not affected: commensalism (b). The epiphytic orchid benefits while the mango tree gets no benefit or harm: commensalism (c). Cuscuta is a parasite deriving nutrition from the host, so the host is harmed: (+, −) (d false). The clown fish gets protection, and the sea anemone does not appear to derive any benefit: (+, 0), not (+, +) (e false).
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) or (e) mislabel parasitism or commensalism; '(b), (c) and (d)' also omits (a).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', populations: population interactions
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
NCERT lists the important components of the functional aspects of an ecosystem, with a pond as its example. Which of the following are among them?

(a) Productivity
(b) Decomposition
(c) Energy flow
(d) Stratification
(e) Species composition

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Structural and functional aspects of an ecosystem
solution.explanation: NCERT: the important components of an ecosystem's function are (i) productivity, (ii) decomposition, (iii) energy flow and (iv) nutrient cycling. Species composition (identification and enumeration of species) and stratification (vertical distribution of species at different levels) are features of an ecosystem's structure.
steps: Functions: productivity, decomposition, energy flow, nutrient cycling
solution.why_others_wrong: Stratification and species composition describe structure, not function, so options with (d) or (e) are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', ecosystem: structure and function
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, the autotrophic components of a pond ecosystem include:

options.text: Zooplankton and the free-swimming and bottom-dwelling animals
Phytoplankton, some algae, and the floating, submerged and marginal plants found at the edges
Fungi, bacteria and flagellates at the bottom of the pond
Only the rooted plants at the edges; phytoplankton are consumers

solution.explanation: NCERT describes the pond: the abiotic component is the water with dissolved inorganic and organic substances and the rich soil deposit at the bottom; the autotrophic components include the phytoplankton, some algae and the floating, submerged and marginal plants found at the edges; the consumers are zooplankton and the free-swimming and bottom-dwelling forms; and the decomposers are fungi, bacteria and flagellates, especially abundant at the bottom.
steps: Autotrophs: phytoplankton, algae, floating, submerged and marginal plants
solution.why_others_wrong: Zooplankton and animals are consumers; fungi, bacteria and flagellates are decomposers; phytoplankton are producers.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', ecosystem: structure and function (pond)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Phytoplankton, some algae, and the floating, submerged and marginal plants found at the edges

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: NCERT's ideal pyramid of energy shows that primary producers convert only about 1 per cent of the energy in the sunlight available to them into net primary productivity.
Statement II: In an energy pyramid, the energy at a lower trophic level is always more than at a higher level.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
