This property, metastasis, is the most feared property of malignant tumours.
steps: Secondary tumours at a distant site -> metastasis
solution.why_others_wrong: Benign tumours stay confined and do not spread, so neither benign option fits; cells that continue to divide and invade have lost, not kept, contact inhibition.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 'Human Health and Disease', Cancer
solution.final_answer: Option A: A malignant tumour showing metastasis

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following human diseases are transmitted through the bite of mosquitoes, according to NCERT?

(a) Malaria
(b) Filariasis
(c) Dengue
(d) Chikungunya
(e) Typhoid

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: malaria (Plasmodium) is transmitted by the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito; filarial worms are transmitted to a healthy person through the bite of female mosquito vectors; the Aedes mosquitoes are the vectors of dengue and chikungunya. Typhoid spreads through food and water contaminated with Salmonella typhi.
solution.why_others_wrong: '(a) and (b) only' leaves out dengue and chikungunya, spread by Aedes; any option with typhoid is wrong, since typhoid spreads through contaminated food and water.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 'Human Health and Disease', Common Diseases in Humans
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Cocaine has a potent stimulating action on the central nervous system, producing a sense of euphoria and increased energy.
Reason (R): Cocaine is obtained from the coca plant Erythroxylum coca, native to South America.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Both are NCERT statements. Cocaine interferes with the transport of the neurotransmitter dopamine and has a potent stimulating action on the CNS. That it comes from a South American plant is a fact about its source; it does not explain why it stimulates the nervous system.
steps: R gives the plant source, not the mechanism -> not the explanation
solution.why_others_wrong: Both statements are true, so options with a false statement are wrong; R is about where cocaine comes from, not about how it acts.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 'Human Health and Disease', Drugs and Alcohol Abuse
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, which of the following can cause DNA damage leading to neoplastic transformation even though it is a NON-ionising radiation?

solution.explanation: NCERT: ionising radiations like X-rays and gamma rays and non-ionising radiations like UV cause DNA damage leading to neoplastic transformation. Of these, UV is the non-ionising one.
steps: Non-ionising carcinogen named by NCERT: UV
solution.why_others_wrong: X-rays and gamma rays are carcinogens but are ionising radiations; tobacco smoke is a chemical carcinogen, not a radiation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 'Human Health and Disease', Cancer (causes of cancer)
solution.final_answer: Option C: UV radiation

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (lymphoid organ) with List-II (NCERT description).

List-I:
A. Bone marrow
B. Thymus
C. Spleen
D. Lymph nodes

List-II:
I. Lobular organ near the heart, beneath the breastbone; quite large at birth and reduces in size with age
II. Small solid structures located at different points along the lymphatic system that trap antigens in lymph and tissue fluid
III. Main lymphoid organ, where all blood cells including lymphocytes are produced
IV. Large bean-shaped organ that filters the blood and is a large reservoir of erythrocytes

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the bone marrow is the main lymphoid organ where all blood cells including lymphocytes are produced; the thymus is a lobular organ located near the heart and beneath the breastbone, quite large at birth but reducing in size with age; the spleen is a large bean-shaped organ that acts as a filter of the blood and has a large reservoir of erythrocytes; lymph nodes are small solid structures located at different points along the lymphatic system that trap micro-organisms or other antigens in the lymph and tissue fluid.
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes exchange the bone marrow with the thymus, the spleen (filters blood) with the lymph nodes (trap antigens in lymph), or the thymus with the spleen.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 'Human Health and Disease', Immunity (lymphoid organs)
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
A woman who has been vaccinated against tetanus gives birth. Her baby receives antibodies against the tetanus toxin through the placenta. Which of the following statements are correct?

(a) At birth, the baby has passive immunity against tetanus.
(b) The baby's own memory B and T-cells against tetanus have been generated by these antibodies.
(c) The antibodies were produced by the mother's immune system, not by the baby's.
(d) Vaccinating the baby later will give it active immunity against tetanus.
(e) The protection the baby has at birth is a form of innate immunity.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: when ready-made antibodies are directly given, it is called passive immunity; the foetus receives some antibodies from the mother through the placenta during pregnancy, an example of passive immunity. Preformed antibodies do not make the receiver produce its own antibodies or memory cells. Active immunity results when the host is exposed to antigens (as in vaccination) and produces its own antibodies, generating memory B and T-cells. Innate immunity is non-specific; antibodies against one toxin are part of acquired immunity.
steps: (b) false - no memory cells from passive transfer
(e) false - antibodies are acquired, specific defence
solution.why_others_wrong: (b) is false because only exposure to antigens, not receiving antibodies, generates memory cells; (e) is false because specific antibodies belong to acquired immunity, not to innate, non-specific defence.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 'Human Health and Disease', Immunity (active and passive immunity; vaccination)
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A town faces outbreaks of malaria, dengue and typhoid. Which single measure from NCERT's list would help to control malaria and dengue but would NOT, by itself, prevent typhoid?

options.text: Consuming only clean drinking water and food
Observing standard practices of hygiene in public catering
Avoiding stagnation of water around homes and regularly cleaning household coolers

solution.concept: Matching control measures to modes of spread
solution.explanation: Malaria and dengue are spread by mosquitoes (Anopheles and Aedes), so NCERT's vector-control measures - avoiding stagnation of water in and around homes, regular cleaning of household coolers, use of mosquito nets, introducing fishes like Gambusia that feed on mosquito larvae, spraying of insecticides - help against both. Typhoid spreads through food and water contaminated with Salmonella typhi, so controlling mosquitoes does not prevent it; clean drinking water and food do.
solution.why_others_wrong: Clean water and food, disposal of excreta and hygiene in catering are measures against diseases spread through contaminated food and water such as typhoid, and they do little against mosquito breeding.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 'Human Health and Disease', Common Diseases in Humans; Prevention and Control of Diseases
solution.final_answer: Option D: Avoiding stagnation of water around homes and regularly cleaning household coolers

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In an AIDS patient, the production of antibodies against new infections becomes weak.
Reason (R): HIV progressively increases the number of helper T-lymphocytes in the infected person.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: T-cells themselves do not secrete antibodies but help B-cells produce them. In HIV infection the number of helper T-lymphocytes progressively DECREASES, and the person becomes unable to produce a proper immune response, including antibody production. So A is true, but R reverses the change in helper T-cells and is false.
steps: A: true - fewer helper T-cells -> less help to B-cells
R: false - helper T-cell number decreases
solution.why_others_wrong: R states an increase where NCERT describes a progressive decrease, so options calling R true are wrong; A is true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 'Human Health and Disease', AIDS; Immunity
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (defect in a person) with List-II (defence that is most directly impaired).

List-I:
A. No functional B-lymphocytes
B. No functional T-lymphocytes
C. No mast cells
D. Virus-infected cells cannot secrete interferons

List-II:
I. Protection of non-infected cells from further viral infection
II. Release of histamine and serotonin in allergic reactions
III. Humoral immune response (antibodies in the blood)
IV. Cell-mediated immunity, such as graft rejection

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: B-lymphocytes produce the antibodies of the humoral immune response; T-lymphocytes mediate cell-mediated immunity, which is responsible for graft rejection; allergic symptoms are due to chemicals like histamine and serotonin released from mast cells; virus-infected cells secrete interferons, which protect non-infected cells from further viral infection.
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes exchange the humoral (B-cell) and cell-mediated (T-cell) responses, exchange mast cells with interferons, or give the allergic reaction to T-cells.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 'Human Health and Disease', Immunity
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
How many of the following are SECONDARY lymphoid organs, according to NCERT?

Spleen, thymus, tonsils, bone marrow, Peyer's patches of the small intestine, appendix, lymph nodes

solution.explanation: NCERT: the primary lymphoid organs are the bone marrow and the thymus, where immature lymphocytes differentiate into antigen-sensitive lymphocytes. The secondary lymphoid organs are the spleen, lymph nodes, tonsils, Peyer's patches of the small intestine and the appendix. From the list: spleen, tonsils, Peyer's patches, appendix and lymph nodes = 5.
steps: Secondary: spleen, tonsils, Peyer's patches, appendix, lymph nodes
solution.why_others_wrong: Four leaves out the appendix (or another secondary organ); six counts the thymus or bone marrow as secondary; seven counts every organ, ignoring that the thymus and bone marrow are primary.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 'Human Health and Disease', Immunity (lymphoid organs)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Five

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A person who has been vaccinated against a pathogen usually does not suffer from the disease on later exposure to that pathogen.
Reason (R): Vaccination generates memory B and T-cells that recognise the pathogen quickly on subsequent exposure and overwhelm the invaders with a massive production of antibodies.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the principle of immunisation or vaccination is based on the property of memory of the immune system. Vaccines generate memory B and T-cells that recognise the pathogen quickly on subsequent exposure and overwhelm the invaders with a massive production of antibodies. That is exactly why the vaccinated person is protected, so R explains A.
steps: R: true - memory cells, quick and massive response
Quick response neutralises the pathogen -> R explains A
solution.why_others_wrong: R is the mechanism of protection by vaccines, so 'R is not the correct explanation' is wrong; neither statement is false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 'Human Health and Disease', Vaccination and Immunisation
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following diseases are acquired mainly by taking in food or water contaminated with the pathogen or its eggs?

(a) Typhoid
(b) Amoebiasis
(c) Ascariasis
(d) Pneumonia
(e) Ringworm

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Diseases spread through contaminated food and water
solution.explanation: NCERT: Salmonella typhi generally enters the small intestine through food and water contaminated with it; drinking water and food contaminated by faecal matter are the main source of Entamoeba infection (amoebiasis); a healthy person acquires Ascaris infection through water, vegetables, fruits, etc., contaminated with its eggs. Pneumonia spreads by inhaling droplets/aerosols released by an infected person, and ringworms are acquired from soil or by using towels, clothes or combs of infected individuals.
steps: (b) amoebiasis: food and water contaminated by faeces
(c) ascariasis: eggs in water, vegetables, fruits
solution.why_others_wrong: '(a) and (b) only' leaves out ascariasis, whose eggs are taken in with contaminated food and water; pneumonia (droplets) and ringworm (soil, towels, combs) are acquired in other ways.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 'Human Health and Disease', Common Diseases in Humans
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Hind II, the first restriction endonuclease whose functioning depended on a specific DNA nucleotide sequence, always cuts DNA molecules at a particular point by recognising a specific sequence of:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the first restriction endonuclease, Hind II, was found to always cut DNA molecules at a particular point by recognising a specific sequence of six base pairs. This specific base sequence is known as the recognition sequence for Hind II.
steps: Hind II: recognition sequence of six base pairs
Cuts at a particular point within that sequence
solution.why_others_wrong: NCERT gives six base pairs for Hind II; the other numbers are not NCERT's figure for this enzyme.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Restriction Enzymes
solution.final_answer: Option D: Six base pairs

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In the E. coli cloning vector pBR322 shown in NCERT, the recognition sites for PstI and PvuI lie within which gene?

solution.explanation: NCERT's map of pBR322 shows the antibiotic resistance genes ampR and tetR, the ori and the rop gene, with restriction sites for Hind III, EcoRI, BamHI, SalI, PvuII, PstI, PvuI and ClaI. BamHI and SalI lie within the tetracycline resistance gene, while PstI and PvuI lie within the ampicillin resistance gene.
solution.why_others_wrong: tetR carries the BamHI and SalI sites; rop codes for proteins involved in replication and ori is where replication starts; neither holds the PstI and PvuI sites in NCERT's map.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Cloning Vectors
solution.final_answer: Option C: The ampicillin resistance gene (ampR)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The progression of a restriction enzyme digestion can be checked by agarose gel electrophoresis.
Reason (R): In agarose gel electrophoresis, smaller DNA fragments move more slowly than larger ones.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: you can check the progression of a restriction enzyme digestion by agarose gel electrophoresis. The DNA fragments separate according to their size through the sieving effect provided by the agarose gel; hence, the smaller the fragment size, the farther it moves. So A is true and R, which reverses this, is false.
steps: R: false - smaller fragments move farther (faster)
solution.why_others_wrong: R reverses the relation between fragment size and distance moved, so options calling R true are wrong; A is NCERT's own line.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Processes of Recombinant DNA Technology (Cutting of DNA; separation of DNA fragments)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a method for introducing recombinant DNA into host cells?

solution.explanation: NCERT: recombinant DNA can be introduced into host cells by making bacteria competent (calcium treatment and heat shock), by micro-injection into the nucleus of an animal cell, by biolistics (gene gun) for plants, and by 'disarmed pathogen' vectors. Elution is the extraction of separated DNA bands cut out from an agarose gel.
steps: Micro-injection, biolistics, disarmed pathogens, competence: DNA transfer methods
Elution: recovering DNA from a gel piece
solution.why_others_wrong: Micro-injection, biolistics and disarmed pathogen vectors are all NCERT's methods of introducing alien DNA into host cells; elution only recovers DNA from a gel.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Competent Host (for transformation with recombinant DNA)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Elution

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A bioreactor provides the optimal conditions for achieving the desired product. Which of the following is NOT among the conditions NCERT lists?

solution.explanation: NCERT: a bioreactor provides the optimal conditions for achieving the desired product by providing optimum growth conditions - temperature, pH, substrate, salts, vitamins and oxygen. Light intensity is not in this list.
steps: NCERT list: temperature, pH, substrate, salts, vitamins, oxygen
solution.why_others_wrong: pH, oxygen and vitamins are all among NCERT's optimum growth conditions provided in a bioreactor.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Processes of Recombinant DNA Technology (Obtaining the foreign gene product)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Light intensity

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Foreign DNA is inserted within the coding sequence of β-galactosidase in a vector that also carries an ampicillin resistance gene, and E. coli is transformed. On a plate containing ampicillin and a chromogenic substrate, 300 colonies grow, of which 240 are blue. How many of the colonies carry recombinant DNA?

solution.explanation: Only transformants grow on ampicillin. NCERT: the presence of a chromogenic substrate gives blue coloured colonies if the plasmid in the bacteria does not have an insert; in the presence of an insert, the β-galactosidase gene is inactivated (insertional inactivation) and the colonies do not produce any colour. So recombinants = 300 - 240 = 60.
solution.why_others_wrong: 240 counts the blue colonies, which carry the vector without the insert; 300 counts every transformant; 180 subtracts the recombinants twice (240 - 60).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Cloning Vectors (insertional inactivation)
solution.final_answer: Option A: 60

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A plasmid vector is cut with EcoRI and a gene of interest is cut out with BamHI. Following NCERT, what is the problem in joining them with DNA ligase?

options.text: The two DNAs do not have the same kind of sticky ends, so they cannot pair and be joined as they are
DNA ligase can join only DNA fragments that have no sticky ends
BamHI produces fragments that cannot be separated on an agarose gel
EcoRI destroys the origin of replication of every vector it cuts

solution.explanation: NCERT: when cut by the same restriction enzyme, the resultant DNA fragments have the same kind of 'sticky ends', and these can be joined together (end-to-end) using DNA ligases. Normally, the vector and the source DNA are therefore cut with the same restriction enzyme. Ends made by two different enzymes such as EcoRI and BamHI are not the same kind of sticky ends.
steps: Same enzyme -> same kind of sticky ends
EcoRI ends and BamHI ends differ -> cannot be joined directly
solution.why_others_wrong: NCERT describes ligase joining fragments with matching sticky ends; BamHI fragments separate on gels like any others; and EcoRI does not destroy the ori of every vector (vectors are chosen with single, suitable sites).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Processes of Recombinant DNA Technology (Insertion of the gene into a vector)
solution.final_answer: Option A: The two DNAs do not have the same kind of sticky ends, so they cannot pair and be joined as they are

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following steps does NCERT describe for making E. coli cells take up a recombinant plasmid?

(a) Treating the cells with a specific concentration of a divalent cation such as calcium
(b) Incubating the cells with the recombinant DNA on ice
(c) Placing them briefly at 42 °C (heat shock)
(d) Putting them back on ice
(e) Treating them with lysozyme first to break open the cells

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: since DNA is hydrophilic, bacterial cells are made 'competent' by treating them with a specific concentration of a divalent cation such as calcium, which increases the efficiency with which DNA enters the bacterium through pores in its cell wall. The cells are incubated with recombinant DNA on ice, then placed briefly at 42 °C (heat shock), and then put back on ice. Lysozyme is used to break open bacterial cells when DNA is to be isolated, which would kill the host.
steps: (e) lysozyme lyses cells - used for DNA isolation
solution.why_others_wrong: Lysozyme breaks open bacterial cells during DNA isolation and has no place in transformation, so options with (e) are wrong; '(b), (c) and (d) only' leaves out the calcium treatment that makes the cells competent.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Competent Host (for transformation with recombinant DNA)
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following must be added to the reaction for amplifying a gene by PCR, as described in NCERT?

(a) The DNA (template) containing the gene
(b) Two sets of primers
(c) A thermostable DNA polymerase
(d) Nucleotides (deoxynucleotides)
(e) A restriction enzyme and DNA ligase

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: in PCR, multiple copies of the gene (or DNA) of interest are synthesised in vitro using two sets of primers and the enzyme DNA polymerase. The enzyme extends the primers using the nucleotides provided in the reaction and the genomic DNA as template. A thermostable DNA polymerase (from Thermus aquaticus) is used. Restriction enzymes and ligase are not part of the amplification itself.
solution.why_others_wrong: '(a), (b) and (c) only' forgets the nucleotides from which the new strands are built; PCR amplification does not use a restriction enzyme or DNA ligase, so options with (e) are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Processes of Recombinant DNA Technology (Amplification of gene of interest using PCR)
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Chitinase is used to break open plant cells during the isolation of DNA.
Reason (R): Cellulase is used to break open plant cells during the isolation of DNA.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: in order to release DNA along with other macromolecules, the cell is broken open by treating it with enzymes such as lysozyme (bacteria), cellulase (plant cells) and chitinase (fungus). So A is false and R is true.
solution.why_others_wrong: Chitinase is NCERT's enzyme for fungal cells, so A is false and options calling it true are wrong; R is correct.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Processes of Recombinant DNA Technology (Isolation of the genetic material)
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (feature of a plasmid used as a cloning vector) with List-II (consequence).

List-I:
A. It lacks an origin of replication
B. It lacks a selectable marker
C. It has several recognition sites for the restriction enzyme to be used
D. The foreign DNA is inserted within its β-galactosidase gene

List-II:
I. Colonies carrying the recombinant DNA give no colour with a chromogenic substrate
II. The plasmid is cut into several fragments, which complicates gene cloning
III. Transformants cannot be identified and separated from non-transformants
IV. The plasmid, with any linked DNA, is not replicated in the host

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: ori is the sequence from where replication starts, and any piece of DNA linked to it can replicate within the host cells; a selectable marker helps in identifying and eliminating non-transformants; the presence of more than one recognition site within the vector will generate several fragments, which will complicate gene cloning; insertion of foreign DNA within the β-galactosidase gene inactivates it, so recombinant colonies do not produce colour with a chromogenic substrate.
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes exchange the roles of ori (replication) and the marker (selection), confuse the marker with the restriction sites, or give the colour result to multiple sites.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Cloning Vectors
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In agarose gel electrophoresis, DNA fragments separate according to their size through the sieving effect provided by the agarose gel.
Statement II: The separated DNA bands are cut out from the gel, and the DNA extracted from them is used in constructing recombinant DNA by joining it with cloning vectors.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Both are NCERT statements. Fragments separate by size through the sieving effect of the agarose gel; the separated bands are cut out and extracted from the gel piece (elution), and the purified DNA fragments are used in constructing recombinant DNA by joining them with cloning vectors.
solution.why_others_wrong: Both statements are NCERT's own, so every option calling either of them false is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Processes of Recombinant DNA Technology (separation and isolation of DNA fragments)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A recombinant protein to be used as a drug has been produced in a bioreactor. Which of the following gives the correct order of the steps that follow, as described in NCERT?

options.text: Clinical trials → separation and purification → formulation with suitable preservatives
Formulation with suitable preservatives → separation and purification → clinical trials
Separation and purification → formulation with suitable preservatives → clinical trials
Separation and purification → clinical trials → isolation of the gene of interest

solution.explanation: NCERT: after completion of the biosynthetic stage, the product has to be subjected through a series of processes before it is ready for marketing as a finished product. The processes include separation and purification, collectively referred to as downstream processing. The product has to be formulated with suitable preservatives, and such formulation has to undergo thorough clinical trials, as in the case of drugs.
solution.why_others_wrong: A product must be separated and purified before it can be formulated, and it is the formulation that undergoes clinical trials; isolating the gene is an early step of recombinant DNA work, not one after production.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Processes of Recombinant DNA Technology (Downstream processing)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Separation and purification → formulation with suitable preservatives → clinical trials

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: EcoRI cuts 5'-GAATTC-3' between G and A on each strand, leaving a single-stranded overhang 5'-AATT-3' on each cut end. When two such ends meet, the overhangs pair with each other. Using the base-pairing rule that A pairs with T through two hydrogen bonds (and G with C through three), how many hydrogen bonds hold the two paired overhangs together at one such joint, before DNA ligase acts?

solution.explanation: The 5'-AATT-3' overhang of one end pairs, antiparallel, with the 5'-AATT-3' overhang of the other end, forming four base pairs, all A-T. Each A-T pair has two hydrogen bonds, so 4 × 2 = 8 hydrogen bonds. NCERT: these hydrogen bonds between sticky ends facilitate the action of DNA ligase.
solution.why_others_wrong: 12 uses three hydrogen bonds per pair (the G-C value); 4 counts one bond per pair; 6 counts only three base pairs.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Restriction Enzymes; Class 12 Ch 5 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', Structure of polynucleotide chain
solution.final_answer: Option B: 8

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A circular plasmid is digested and run on an agarose gel. With EcoRI alone, one band of 5 kb is seen. With BamHI alone, one band of 5 kb is seen. With EcoRI and BamHI together, two bands of 2 kb and 3 kb are seen. What can be concluded?

options.text: The plasmid is 10 kb, with two EcoRI sites and two BamHI sites
Neither enzyme cuts the plasmid, since one band is seen with each
The plasmid is 5 kb with two EcoRI sites, 2 kb apart, and no BamHI site
The plasmid is 5 kb, with one EcoRI site and one BamHI site that are 2 kb apart one way round the circle and 3 kb apart the other

solution.explanation: A circular DNA cut at n sites gives n fragments. One 5 kb band with each enzyme alone means each enzyme cuts the 5 kb circle once (opening it into a 5 kb linear molecule). Cutting with both gives two fragments, 2 kb and 3 kb, so the EcoRI and BamHI sites are 2 kb apart on one side of the circle and 3 kb apart on the other. Smaller fragments move farther in the gel, so the 2 kb band lies farther from the well.
steps: Single digests: one site each, plasmid = 5 kb
Sites are 2 kb apart one way round and 3 kb the other
solution.why_others_wrong: Two sites per enzyme in a circle would give two fragments with each enzyme alone; an uncut plasmid would not give a linear 5 kb band whose double digest splits into 2 + 3 kb; and if BamHI had no site, the double digest would match the EcoRI digest.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Processes of Recombinant DNA Technology (Cutting of DNA; separation of DNA fragments)
solution.final_answer: Option D: The plasmid is 5 kb, with one EcoRI site and one BamHI site that are 2 kb apart one way round the circle and 3 kb apart the other

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
A scientist wants to introduce a recombinant gene into PLANT cells. Which of the following methods described in NCERT are suitable?

(a) Biolistics (gene gun), using gold or tungsten micro-particles coated with DNA
(b) A 'disarmed' Ti plasmid of Agrobacterium tumefaciens
(c) Micro-injection, which NCERT describes for injecting DNA into the nucleus of an animal cell
(d) A disarmed retrovirus
(e) Calcium treatment followed by heat shock, as used for bacteria

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Choosing a gene-transfer method for plants
solution.explanation: NCERT: biolistics or gene gun is suitable for plants; the Ti plasmid of Agrobacterium tumefaciens has been modified into a cloning vector that is no longer pathogenic to plants but delivers genes of interest into a variety of plants. Micro-injection is described for animal cells, retroviruses have been disarmed to deliver genes into animal cells, and calcium treatment with heat shock is the method for making bacteria competent.
solution.why_others_wrong: NCERT describes micro-injection and disarmed retroviruses for animal cells and calcium plus heat shock for bacteria, so options containing (c), (d) or (e) are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Competent Host (for transformation with recombinant DNA); Cloning Vectors (vectors for cloning genes in plants and animals)
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a) and (b) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (DNA digested completely with one restriction enzyme) with List-II (number of fragments obtained).

List-I:
A. A linear DNA with one recognition site
B. A circular plasmid with one recognition site
C. A linear DNA with three recognition sites
D. A circular plasmid with three recognition sites

List-II:
I. One
II. Two
III. Three
IV. Four

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Counting fragments from linear and circular DNA
solution.explanation: Cutting a linear molecule at n sites gives n + 1 fragments; cutting a circle at n sites gives n fragments. So: linear, 1 site -> 2; circular, 1 site -> 1 (the circle is only opened); linear, 3 sites -> 4; circular, 3 sites -> 3.
steps: A -> II, B -> I, C -> IV, D -> III
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes use the circular rule (n) for linear DNA, the linear rule (n + 1) for circular DNA, or both mistakes together.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Restriction Enzymes
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): If the denaturation step of a PCR cycle is omitted, the primers cannot anneal to the template DNA.
Reason (R): In PCR, the double-stranded DNA is separated into single strands at high temperature (denaturation), and the primers then bind to complementary regions of the single-stranded template.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: each PCR cycle has three steps: denaturation, annealing and extension. Denaturation separates the double-stranded DNA; the primers (small chemically synthesised oligonucleotides complementary to regions of the template) then anneal to the single-stranded DNA. Without denaturation the template remains double-stranded and the primers cannot bind, so R explains A.
steps: No denaturation -> no annealing -> R explains A
solution.why_others_wrong: R states why primers need the denaturation step, so 'R is not the correct explanation' is wrong; neither statement is false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Processes of Recombinant DNA Technology (Amplification of gene of interest using PCR)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Starting from a single double-stranded DNA molecule, 10 PCR cycles in which the DNA doubles every cycle give 1024 molecules.
Statement II: On an agarose gel, a 0.5 kb DNA fragment moves a shorter distance from the well than a 5 kb fragment.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Statement I: 1 × 2¹⁰ = 1024 molecules, so it is true. Statement II: NCERT - the smaller the fragment size, the farther it moves; the 0.5 kb fragment moves farther than the 5 kb fragment, so Statement II is false.
steps: II: smaller fragments move farther -> false
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement II reverses the size-mobility relation, so options calling it true are wrong; the arithmetic in Statement I is correct.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Processes of Recombinant DNA Technology (PCR; separation of DNA fragments)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT one of the reasons NCERT gives for producing transgenic animals?

To increase the speed of locomotion of farm animals

Locomotion speed: not a listed reason

Match List-I (term) with List-II (meaning).

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: Bt stands for Bacillus thuringiensis; the Bt toxin is coded by a gene cry, and there are a number of them (e.g., cryIAc, cryIIAb, cryIAb); RNAi involves silencing of a specific mRNA due to a complementary dsRNA molecule that binds to and prevents translation of the mRNA; plants, bacteria, fungi and animals whose genes have been altered by manipulation are called genetically modified organisms (GMO).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Insulin consists of two short polypeptide chains, chain A and chain B, that are linked together by disulphide bridges.
Reason (R): In Eli Lilly's method, a single gene for pro-insulin was expressed in E. coli and the C peptide was then removed.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Structure and production of human insulin
solution.explanation: NCERT: insulin consists of two short polypeptide chains, chain A and chain B, linked together by disulphide bridges, so A is true. In 1983, Eli Lilly prepared two DNA sequences corresponding to the A and B chains, introduced them into plasmids of E. coli to produce the chains separately, and combined the extracted chains by creating disulphide bonds. R, which describes a single pro-insulin gene, is false.
steps: R: false - separate DNA sequences for chains A and B
solution.why_others_wrong: R misdescribes Eli Lilly's method, so options calling R true are wrong; A is NCERT's description of insulin.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 'Biotechnology and its Applications', Biotechnological Applications in Medicine (Genetically Engineered Insulin)

Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

solution.why_others_wrong: Both statements are correct NCERT lines, so every option calling either of them false is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 'Biotechnology and its Applications', Transgenic Animals

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A company uses E. coli to produce only chain A of human insulin and markets it as insulin. Based on NCERT, why would this product not be functional insulin?

options.text: Chain A must first be converted into DNA inside the patient
Functional insulin needs both chain A and chain B, joined by disulphide bridges
Insulin made in bacteria is always pig insulin, which causes allergy
Chain A is the C peptide, which is removed from mature insulin

solution.explanation: NCERT: insulin consists of two short polypeptide chains, chain A and chain B, linked together by disulphide bridges. In Eli Lilly's method, chains A and B were produced separately, extracted and combined by creating disulphide bonds to form human insulin. Chain A alone lacks chain B and the disulphide links, so it is not insulin.
steps: Functional insulin = chain A + chain B
solution.why_others_wrong: Proteins are not converted into DNA; recombinant human insulin is human, not pig, insulin; and the C peptide is a separate stretch of the pro-hormone, not chain A.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 'Biotechnology and its Applications', Biotechnological Applications in Medicine (Genetically Engineered Insulin)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Functional insulin needs both chain A and chain B, joined by disulphide bridges

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
According to NCERT, which of the following are advantages of therapeutic drugs produced by recombinant DNA technology?

(a) They can be mass-produced.
(b) They are safe and more effective.
(c) They do not induce the unwanted immunological responses that are common with similar products isolated from non-human sources.
(d) They have to be extracted from the pancreas of slaughtered animals.
(e) Recombinant insulin is cattle insulin made in bacteria.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: recombinant DNA technological processes have made immense impact in healthcare by enabling mass production of safe and more effective therapeutic drugs; further, recombinant therapeutics do not induce unwanted immunological responses, as is common in the case of similar products isolated from non-human sources. Extraction from slaughtered animals is the older method, and recombinant insulin is human insulin.
solution.why_others_wrong: '(a) and (b) only' leaves out the absence of unwanted immune responses; extraction from animal pancreas (d) is what recombinant production replaced, and the insulin made is human insulin, not cattle insulin (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 'Biotechnology and its Applications', Biotechnological Applications in Medicine
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
A child with adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency is given gene therapy using his own lymphocytes. Which of the following statements are correct?

(a) The enzyme ADA is crucial for the immune system to function.
(b) Lymphocytes from the patient's blood are grown in a culture outside the body.
(c) A functional ADA cDNA is introduced into these lymphocytes using a retroviral vector.
(d) Retroviruses used as vectors for animal cells are disarmed before use.
(e) Once infused, the engineered lymphocytes are immortal, so a single infusion cures the child.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT (Ch 10): ADA is crucial for the immune system to function; in gene therapy, lymphocytes from the blood of the patient are grown in a culture outside the body, a functional ADA cDNA is introduced into them using a retroviral vector, and the cells are returned to the patient; as these cells are not immortal, the patient requires periodic infusion. NCERT (Ch 9): retroviruses, which can transform normal cells into cancerous cells, have been disarmed and are now used to deliver desirable genes into animal cells.
steps: (e) false - cells are not immortal; periodic infusion needed
solution.why_others_wrong: (e) is false because NCERT says the engineered lymphocytes are not immortal; '(a), (b) and (c) only' leaves out (d), which is NCERT's statement that retroviral vectors are disarmed.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 'Biotechnology and its Applications', Gene Therapy; Class 12 Ch 9, Cloning Vectors
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A diabetic patient who is allergic to insulin extracted from the pancreas of pigs can usually be treated with human insulin produced by recombinant DNA technology.
Reason (R): Recombinant therapeutics do not induce the unwanted immunological responses that are common with similar products isolated from non-human sources.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

solution.concept: Why recombinant human insulin avoids allergy
solution.explanation: NCERT: insulin from slaughtered cattle and pigs caused some patients to develop allergy or other types of reactions to the foreign protein. Recombinant therapeutics do not induce unwanted immunological responses, as is common with products from non-human sources. That is why recombinant human insulin suits such a patient, so R explains A.
steps: Pig insulin = foreign protein -> allergy in some patients
Recombinant human insulin: no unwanted immune response
solution.why_others_wrong: R is the reason the switch to recombinant insulin helps, so 'R is not the correct explanation' is wrong; neither statement is false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 'Biotechnology and its Applications', Biotechnological Applications in Medicine (Genetically Engineered Insulin)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

NCERT also names several crops besides cotton in which Bt toxin genes have been expressed: corn, rice, tomato, potato and soyabean.

Match List-I (item) with List-II (what NCERT says about it).

Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.

solution.explanation: NCERT gives golden rice, i.e., vitamin A enriched rice, as an example of a GM crop with enhanced nutritional value. It is not described as a Bt (insect-resistant) crop; insect resistance comes from cry genes of Bacillus thuringiensis. So A is false and R is true.
steps: A: false - golden rice is about nutrition, not Bt toxin
R: true - enriched in vitamin A

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A virus with an RNA genome infects a eukaryotic cell. According to NCERT's account of RNA interference as a method of cellular defence, how could the cell limit the virus?

options.text: The cell could produce Bt toxin, which creates pores in the virus
The cell could cut the viral RNA with EcoRI at GAATTC sites
The cell could produce interferons that make the infected cell immortal
A complementary dsRNA molecule could bind to the specific viral mRNA and prevent its translation (silencing)

solution.explanation: NCERT: RNAi takes place in all eukaryotic organisms as a method of cellular defence. This method involves silencing of a specific mRNA due to a complementary dsRNA molecule that binds to and prevents translation of the mRNA (silencing). The source of this complementary RNA could be an infection by viruses having RNA genomes, or mobile genetic elements (transposons) that replicate via an RNA intermediate.
steps: Viral RNA infection can provide the complementary RNA
Translation of that mRNA is prevented -> silencing
solution.why_others_wrong: Bt toxin acts on insect midgut cells, not on viruses; EcoRI is a bacterial enzyme that cuts DNA, not a eukaryotic defence acting on RNA; and interferons protect non-infected cells, they do not make cells immortal.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 'Biotechnology and its Applications', Biotechnological Applications in Agriculture (RNA interference)
solution.final_answer: Option D: A complementary dsRNA molecule could bind to the specific viral mRNA and prevent its translation (silencing)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements correctly compare insulin made in the human body with the human insulin produced by Eli Lilly?

(a) In the body, insulin is synthesised as a pro-hormone containing an extra stretch called the C peptide.
(b) Eli Lilly produced chains A and B separately in E. coli.
(c) In both cases, the functional hormone has chains A and B linked by disulphide bonds.
(d) Eli Lilly had to remove the C peptide from the chains made in E. coli.
(e) Eli Lilly introduced DNA sequences corresponding to the A and B chains into plasmids of E. coli.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: in mammals, including humans, insulin is synthesised as a pro-hormone that contains an extra stretch called the C peptide, which is removed during maturation. Eli Lilly prepared two DNA sequences corresponding to the A and B chains, introduced them into plasmids of E. coli to produce the chains separately, and combined the extracted chains by creating disulphide bonds. Since no pro-hormone was made, there was no C peptide to remove.
steps: (c) true - A and B linked by disulphide bonds
(d) false - no pro-insulin made, no C peptide
solution.why_others_wrong: (d) is false because Eli Lilly's chains were made separately, not as pro-insulin, so options with (d) are wrong; '(b), (c) and (e) only' leaves out the natural pro-hormone with its C peptide.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 'Biotechnology and its Applications', Biotechnological Applications in Medicine (Genetically Engineered Insulin)
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b), (c) and (e) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency affects the functioning of the immune system.
Reason (R): The first clinical gene therapy was given in 1990 to a 4-year-old girl with ADA deficiency.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Transgenic mice are being developed for use in testing the safety of the polio vaccine; if successful, they could replace the use of monkeys for testing the safety of batches of the vaccine.
Statement II: Transgenic animals made more sensitive to toxic substances than non-transgenic animals take longer to give the results of toxicity testing.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

steps: Statement II: false - results in less time

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A company develops a commercial product from a medicinal plant of a developing country and the traditional knowledge of its people. It does so with proper authorisation from the country and the people concerned and makes the agreed compensatory payment to them. According to NCERT's definition, is this biopiracy?

options.text: No, because biopiracy refers to use without proper authorisation and without compensatory payment
Yes, because any commercial use of bio-resources of another country is biopiracy
Yes, because only industrialised nations may use bio-resources
No, because medicinal plants are not bio-resources

solution.explanation: NCERT: biopiracy is the term used to refer to the use of bio-resources by multinational companies and other organisations without proper authorisation from the countries and people concerned, without compensatory payment. Here both authorisation and compensation are present, so by NCERT's definition it is not biopiracy.
steps: Biopiracy = use without authorisation AND without compensatory payment
solution.why_others_wrong: NCERT's definition depends on the absence of authorisation and compensation, not on commercial use as such; nothing in NCERT restricts the use of bio-resources to industrialised nations; and medicinal plants are bio-resources, which is why turmeric and neem appear in NCERT's discussion.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 'Biotechnology and its Applications', Ethical Issues
solution.final_answer: Option A: No, because biopiracy refers to use without proper authorisation and without compensatory payment
